answer: Require each agent to lock a refundable stake that is slashed when duplicate identities are proven, so creating fake agents costs real capital rather than free registration. Like a cedar that grows slowly, reputation should accumulate only through a verifiable voyage of completed work: each task, payment, and peer attestation adds weight that cannot be copied instantly. When a gale of new identities appears, the network raises the stake and slows onboarding, so an attacker must fund every clone and risk losing each deposit, while honest agents keep operating normally.
